______________________________ 
 
RESOLUTION: 
 
MLA BEREZA – Addressing Manitoba’s Mental Health Crisis 
 
17. WHEREAS those in this Chamber acknowledge that mental health is a key factor in the overall 
health and well-being of Manitobans; and 
 
WHEREAS in recent years the number of Manitobans experiencing mental health challenges has 
increased significantly, with the sharpest rise occurring among children and youth; and 
 
WHEREAS mental health challenges have been further exacerbated in recent years, and families 
are calling for access to services; and 
 
WHEREAS mental health-related concerns now account for approximately one-third of emergency 
room visits, placing significant strain on acute-care services; and 
 
WHEREAS families seeking timely mental health supports are increasingly forced to turn to private 
services at significant personal cost due to gaps in the public system; and 
 
WHEREAS rural, northern, and remote communities in Manitoba face persistent shortages of 
psychiatrists, psychologists, psychiatric nurses, and other frontline professionals, resulting in unacceptable 
delays in access to assessment and treatment; and 
 
WHEREAS mental health challenges are closely linked to rising rates of homelessness, addictions, 
and justice system involvement, demonstrating the cost of failing to provide early and adequate 
intervention; and 
 
WHEREAS Manitoba continues to have the highest per capita rate of children in care in Canada, 
with over 10,000 children currently in care, and evidence shows that approximately two- thirds of these 
children experience significant mental health challenges; and 
 
WHEREAS despite these realities, mental health infrastructure in the province has not kept pace 
with the growing need; and 
 
  
=====PAGE
 6 
WHEREAS despite growing demand, Manitoba has not yet implemented a comprehensive, 
province-wide mental health strategy with clear benchmarks, measurable wait -time reduction targets, and 
transparent public reporting. 
 
 THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Legislative Assembly of Manitoba urge the Provincial 
Government to develop, present, and implement a comprehensive provincial mental health strategy, with a 
particular focus on children and youth.
